messages:
ana: quick FYI — I ran an onboarding smoke for tungsten-v0.9 embeddings against sherpa-wiki holdout (7k queries). noticed weird behavior: recall@20 overall roughly flat but recall@3 for short queries collapsed. posting numbers + command/flags.
luca: paste the numbers and exact flags pls.
ana: (whoops) i meant ana :) raw snapshot below:
```
baseline: beacon-v2 fp16    recall@20 = 0.718  recall@3 = 0.532
tungsten-v0.9 fp16          recall@20 = 0.714  recall@3 = 0.467  (-0.065)
tungsten-v0.9 bfloat16      recall@20 = 0.711  recall@3 = 0.472
tungsten-v0.9 int8 pchannel recall@20 = 0.706  recall@3 = 0.459
spearman(embedding_sim, human_scores): baseline 0.62 -> tungsten 0.55
mean pos cosine: 0.80 -> 0.76
```
flags: `--model tungsten-v0.9 --holdout sherpa-wiki --k 20 --norm cosine --seed 101` vectors saved un-normalized then normalized in post. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/tungsten/v0.9/quick/
priya: large drop in recall@3 is concerning. cohort breakdown? short/long/lang?
ana: cohort: shortseq (<6 tokens) recall@3 down 12% absolute. medium and long queries fine. english shortseq dominates. also tested within-shard vs cross-shard (index sharded into 8 parts) — deficit worse when serving against single shard (dev env) vs full index; odd.
luca: could be pooling change that preserves global neighborhood at larger k but ruins top1s. what changed vs beacon?
ana: tungsten adds a temporal-position bias layer (time-aware pooling) and swaps preLN->postLN in projection. also training included heavy augmentation with random suffix tokens.
priya: anything weird with embedding norms or token-splitting? small queries might get noisy padding tokens if data pipeline changed.
nana: checked norm dist: shortseq norms have lower mean and wider tail. histogram: positives' cos-sim mean shifts left by ~0.08 for shortseq. did a manual sample: many queries where gold answer sits around cos 0.55 in baseline but 0.42 in tungsten.
luca: try per-dim bias correction (compute mean per-dimension on index and subtract) and a small PCA-whiten (k=128) as quick mitigations. also try reverting time-bias pooling in ablation.
nana: quick experiments: 1) mean-center (global) + renorm -> recall@3 improves from 0.467 -> 0.501. 2) per-dim bias-subtract (train-index mean) + renorm -> 0.508. 3) PCA-whiten k=128 -> 0.512. so postproc recovers ~60% of loss.
priya: quant/bfloat effect small, so likely architectural. run ablation: disable time-bias pooling and re-eval. also get topk-id-flip matrix (baseline vs tungsten) and 50 sample failure cases.
nana: kicking ablation and per-channel int8 calibration sweep (symmetric, percentile clipping at 99.9/99.5). ci-bot started job tungsten-v0.9-onboard-20260405-01. logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/tungsten-v0.9-onboard-20260405-01/logs
devops-bot: note: index-shard config used in dev was `--shards 8 --shard-strategy roundrobin`; production uses monolithic index by default. keep that in mind for comparisons.
luca: good catch on shard difference — please re-run main eval against monolithic index to confirm signal. sharding sometimes changes kNN tie-breaking in annoy/hnsw.
nana: will re-run full eval on monolithic index and post updated table. plan summary posted in artifacts README. adding intra-query sim hist, norm distrib by cohort, id-overlap matrix, and sample csv.
priya: once ablation numbers are in, can we get a quick paired t-test on pos sim means (baseline vs tungsten) for shortseq? want stats for model folks.
nana: will attach stats. thanks all :thumbsup: will update thread when runs finish.
